items.anchor: Flat contour segments are allowed in this finite parabolic family.
items.note: Both sentences of line 3. The example family (a member of the finite parabolic family) has, at every positive level t, the vertical segment {(sqrt(t/3), v) : -t/3 <= v <= 2t/3} in the level set {F = t} on the boundary of the sublevel {F <= t}, which is therefore not strictly convex: the strict-contour hypothesis of the planar theorem (strictly convex positive sublevels, 09_C.tex:47, also in its local form for low sublevels) fails at every positive level, while every admissible run converges by the theorem of this chapter. Non-vacuity of the "every run" conclusion: admissible runs on the example objective exist from every point of differentiability, for every H_0 and 0 < c_1 < c_2 < 1 (example_run_exists, from AdmissibleRunExistence.exists_admissible_run; exampleRun_nonempty), and example_flat_contour applies to them (example after exampleRun_nonempty).

resolved_discrepancies.description: The cross-references of the chapter use the numbering of its source note (bfgs_lean_stage1/master_report/latex/chapters/Q.tex), not the chapter's. Six equation references: "Equation (11) proves (V)" (line 115) means (10.11); "By (12)" (line 136) means (10.12); "By (13)" (line 169) means (10.13); "the second vanishes by (7)" and "proving (16)" (line 198) mean (10.7) and (10.16); "An especially simple scaling for (8)" (line 238) means (10.8). In the companion's numbering (\theequation = ModuleTag.arabic) no equation is numbered (7), (8), (11), (12), (13) or (16): the chapter's displays are tagged (10.7)-(10.18), and the six references print literally, in Sections 10.5.2-10.6, printed pages 62-64 (PDF pages 68-70) of the built companion companion/build/master.pdf of 14 October: "(11)", "(12)" on page 62, "(13)", "(7)", "(16)" on page 63, "(8)" on page 64. Cause: editorial/generate_companion.py:69 replaces the module letter only in Q.-prefixed tags (\tag{Q.12} -> (10.12)), and the source writes these six references without the prefix (Q.tex:101, 118, 147, 176 twice, 212). The mathematics holds with the intended references: secant_visibility ((V) from (10.11)), radial_error (from (10.12)), multiplier_estimates (from (10.13)), segment_bound_facts (the vanishing from (10.7)), branch_change ((10.16)), example_scale (the example's scale has the form (10.8)). The same kind of slip as M17 (Chapter H).
resolved_discrepancies.proposed: Intended text of companion/chapters/10_Q.tex: (10.11) instead of (11) at line 115; (10.12) instead of (12) at line 136; (10.13) instead of (13) at line 169; (10.7) and (10.16) instead of (7) and (16) at line 198; (10.8) instead of (8) at line 238. Fix location: the chapter is generated, so not by hand. Add to editorial/generate_companion.py a logged module-Q transformation (a transform_log entry), applied to the source text before the numbering loop of lines 68-69, that adds the missing prefix: '(11)' -> '(Q.11)' (Q.tex:101), '(12)' -> '(Q.12)' (Q.tex:118), '(13)' -> '(Q.13)' (Q.tex:147), '(7)' -> '(Q.7)' and '(16)' -> '(Q.16)' (Q.tex:176), '(8)' -> '(Q.8)' (Q.tex:212), each occurring exactly once in Q.tex (assert the counts); the existing substitution at line 69 then prints (10.11), (10.12), (10.13), (10.7), (10.16), (10.8). Then regenerate (python3 editorial/generate_companion.py), rebuild the companion and inspect Sections 10.5.2-10.6, printed pages 62-64.
